\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\title{M11: Two-user NOMA with arbitrary fixed QoS}
\author{Internal benchmark model; selected idea-01}
\date{P4 draft for independent review and G4; no simulation results}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Scope, normalization and physical model}
This is an established-method dry run under approved G1--G3, not an
originality claim. Every statement below concerns a single constant-channel
block. Parameters are finite real numbers with
\(P\geq0\), \(0\leq g_w\leq g_s\), and fixed individual targets
\(q_w,q_s\geq0\) in bit/s/Hz over the whole block. No fading distribution,
physical deployment, numerical tolerance or experimental protocol is selected.
Noise variance and bandwidth are normalized to one. Thus \(P\) is linear
transmit power relative to normalized noise, not a dBm input or a physical
power value in watts; \(A=Pg_w\), \(B=Pg_s\) are dimensionless received
SNRs if a user receives full power. No unreported path-loss or SNR conversion
is used. Let scalar complex channels satisfy \(g_i=|h_i|^2\), for
\(i\in\{w,s\}\). Perfect instantaneous CSI and ideal SIC are scoped
idealizations. Independent unit-energy Gaussian codebook symbols \(s_w,s_s\)
give the information-theoretic rate model, not a finite-modulation link model.
Receiver noise \(z_i\sim\mathcal{CN}(0,1)\) has real and imaginary
variance \(1/2\). The full-range strong-user power fraction is
\(a\in[0,1]\); its weak-user counterpart is \(1-a\). The signal equations are
\begin{align}
 x&=\sqrt{P(1-a)}s_w+\sqrt{Pa}s_s, & y_i&=h_ix+z_i.
\end{align}
The average transmitted power is \(P\). An endpoint can carry a zero-rate
message with zero allocated power. There is no constraint \(a\leq1/2\),
SIC margin, residual interference, adaptive time split or altered objective.

\section{Both weak-message decoding sites and rates}
The weak receiver treats the strong message as noise. The strong receiver
first decodes the weak message while treating its own message as noise,
then removes the decoded weak message exactly. Their weak-message SINRs are
\begin{align}
 \gamma_{w\to w}(a)&=\frac{(1-a)A}{1+aA}, &
 \gamma_{w\to s}(a)&=\frac{(1-a)B}{1+aB}, &
 \gamma_{s\to s}(a)&=aB.
\end{align}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_{w\to s}-\gamma_{w\to w}
 =\frac{(1-a)(B-A)}{(1+aA)(1+aB)}\geq0.
\end{equation}
The weak code rate must not exceed either weak-message decoding capacity;
their minimum equals the weak receiver's capacity even at equal gains and
endpoints. Hence the achievable boundary rates and objective are
\begin{align}
 R_w(a)&=\log_2\frac{1+A}{1+aA}, &R_s(a)&=\log_2(1+aB),\\
 F(a)&=R_w(a)+R_s(a).
\end{align}
Choosing a smaller actual code rate is permitted, but cannot improve the
sum-rate maximum. Capacity equalities are ideal asymptotic achievable-rate
limits; no finite-block error probability or practical SIC claim is inferred.
Both target inequalities use \(\geq\), so equality is feasible in exact
real arithmetic.

\section{Exact QoS feasible set, including zero cases}
Define \(T_i=2^{q_i}-1\). For \(B>0\), strong QoS is exactly
\(a\geq T_s/B\). For \(A>0\), weak QoS is exactly
\begin{equation}
 (1-a)A\geq T_w(1+aA)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a\leq\frac{A-T_w}{A(1+T_w)}.
\end{equation}
These follow by applying a strictly increasing logarithm and multiplying
strictly positive denominators; SIC imposes no additional bound because
the second weak decoding site has no smaller capacity.
Use the following branches, without division by zero:
\begin{itemize}
 \item If \(B=0\), ordering also gives \(A=0\). Feasible iff
 \(q_w=q_s=0\), with feasible set \([0,1]\); otherwise infeasible.
 \item If \(A=0<B\), feasible weak QoS requires \(q_w=0\).
 Then set \(L=T_s/B\), \(U=1\).
 \item If \(A>0\) (therefore \(B>0\)), set
 \(L=T_s/B\), \(U=\min\{1,(A-T_w)/(A(1+T_w))\}\).
\end{itemize}
For either positive-\(B\) branch, the set is \(\mathcal A=[L,U]\)
iff \(L\leq U\); otherwise it is empty. Nonnegative targets ensure
\(L\geq0\) and \(U\leq1\). A negative \(U\), \(L>1\), or
\(L>U\) is infeasibility, not an instruction to clamp an answer into
\([0,1]\). For \(A>0\) an equivalent complete feasibility condition is
\begin{equation}
 \frac{T_s}{B}+\frac{T_w}{A}+\frac{T_wT_s}{B}\leq1.
\end{equation}
A singleton \(L=U\) is feasible. Zero total power, zero strong gain,
and both zero gains all enter the \(A=B=0\) branch. Zero weak gain at
positive received strong SNR enters the second branch. Zero QoS gives
the corresponding inactive bound: \(T_s=0\) implies \(L=0\);
\(T_w=0\) implies \(U=1\). Arbitrarily large finite targets can simply
make the interval empty; they are not restricted to paper-specific regimes.

\section{Optimizer, curvature and degeneracies}
\begin{theorem}[Exact scalar solution]
If the feasible set is nonempty, \(a^\star=U\) is a maximizer (use
\(U=1\) in the all-zero branch). If \(B>A\), it is the unique maximizer.
If \(B=A\), every feasible split is optimal. An empty set has no optimizer
and no constrained optimum sum rate.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
On \([0,1]\), direct differentiation gives
\begin{align}
 F'(a)&=\frac{1}{\ln2}\left(\frac{B}{1+aB}-\frac{A}{1+aA}\right)
       =\frac{B-A}{\ln2(1+aA)(1+aB)},\\
 F''(a)&=\frac{1}{\ln2}\left(\frac{A^2}{(1+aA)^2}
                              -\frac{B^2}{(1+aB)^2}\right)\\
 &=-\frac{(B-A)(A+B+2aAB)}{\ln2(1+aA)^2(1+aB)^2}.
\end{align}
Positive denominators give monotonicity; if \(B>A\), then \(B>0\)
and both the first derivative is strictly positive and second derivative
strictly negative. Consequently the largest feasible split is the unique
maximum, including a singleton. If \(B=A\), \(F(a)=\log_2(1+A)\)
is constant. This includes \(A=B=0\), when every rate is zero.
\end{proof}
For \(A>0\), the selected endpoint exactly meets weak QoS,
\(R_w(U)=q_w\), including \(q_w=0,U=1\). For \(A=0<B\),
\(U=1\) gives weak rate zero and strong rate \(\log_2(1+B)\).
Equal gains do not imply equal user rates or equal targets; they only
make the sum constant on the feasible interval. For \(A=B>0\), feasibility
is equivalently \(q_w+q_s\leq\log_2(1+A)\).

The reduced optimization is maximization of a concave scalar function over
an interval, equivalently convex minimization of \(-F\). Strict concavity
holds only for \(B>A\). The weak rate alone is convex and nonincreasing
in \(a\), and the strong rate is concave and nondecreasing; their QoS
sets become affine interval inequalities by exact algebra. No claim of
joint convexity in channels, targets or total power is made. There are
no alternating blocks or iterative convergence claims. Endpoint evaluation
requires a constant number of real-arithmetic operations and elementary
functions, hence \(O(1)\) work and storage per block in that model.
This is not constant bit complexity or constant floating-point latency.

\section{Matched equal-time OMA and conditional comparison}
OMA serves each user for half the same block, using all the same bandwidth
and transmit power \(P\) while active, with the same channels and targets.
It has
\begin{align}
 R_w^{O}&=\tfrac12\log_2(1+A), &R_s^{O}&=\tfrac12\log_2(1+B), &
 F^O&=R_w^O+R_s^O.
\end{align}
OMA is feasible iff \(R_i^O\geq q_i\) for both users, equivalently
\(A\geq2^{2q_w}-1\) and \(B\geq2^{2q_s}-1\).
The baseline rate is per whole block, not per active slot. If block duration
is \(\tau\), both schemes spend normalized energy \(P\tau\):
NOMA transmits at \(P\) throughout, OMA uses \(P\) in each disjoint
half-slot. Neither OMA user uses \(2P\) or \(P/2\). Both occupy one
bandwidth-block resource; noise bandwidth stays one during an active slot.
No optimized OMA scheduling or hardware/CSI/SIC overhead adjustment is included.

\begin{theorem}[Scope-wide OMA inclusion and sum comparison]
With this model and matched reference, OMA feasibility implies NOMA
feasibility. On the both-feasible set, \(F(a^\star)\geq F^O\).
Equality occurs iff \(A=B\); if \(B>A\), the sum inequality is strict.
These conclusions need no fading distribution or high-SNR approximation.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
First suppose \(A>0\). Let \(c(v)=1/(1+\sqrt{1+v})\) for
\(v\geq0\). This function is decreasing, so \(c(B)\leq c(A)\).
Solving the two individual inequalities against their OMA rates gives
\(a\leq c(A)\) for the weak user and \(a\geq c(B)\) for the strong.
The witness \(a_F=c(A)\) therefore attains
\(R_w(a_F)=R_w^O\) and \(R_s(a_F)\geq R_s^O\).
If OMA meets the fixed targets, this same witness meets them too, so it
belongs to \(\mathcal A\). Optimality gives
\(F(a^\star)\geq F(a_F)\geq F^O\). When \(B>A\),
\(c(A)>c(B)\) and the strong inequality is strict since \(B>0\).
For \(A=0<B\), OMA feasibility forces \(q_w=0\), and the separate
witness \(a_F=1\) gives \(R_w=R_w^O=0\) and
\(R_s=\log_2(1+B)>R_s^O\); it also meets \(q_s\).
For \(A=B=0\), OMA feasibility requires both targets zero and the
all-zero NOMA branch is feasible with equal zero sums. Finally if
\(A=B>0\), every feasible NOMA sum is \(\log_2(1+A)=F^O\).
\end{proof}
The fairness witness is a proof device, not a substituted objective,
new QoS choice, or selected implementation split. A sum-optimal split may
give the weak user less than its OMA rate when its fixed target is lower
than that OMA rate. No individual-rate dominance is asserted for the
optimizer. The theorem says nothing about arbitrary fixed NOMA splits,
unmatched OMA, imperfect SIC/CSI, finite-block coding or other scopes.

\section{Feasibility ledger and prospective validation}
For a later ensemble of \(N\) matched blocks, let \(I_N(j),I_O(j)\)
be feasibility indicators, and \(n_{uv}\) count blocks with
\((I_N,I_O)=(u,v)\), \(u,v\in\{0,1\}\). Report all four counts,
\(N=\sum_{u,v}n_{uv}\), NOMA fraction \((n_{10}+n_{11})/N\),
OMA fraction \((n_{01}+n_{11})/N\), and paired count \(n_{11}\).
The exact theorem predicts \(n_{01}=0\); a numerical positive count
requires diagnosis, not deletion. Fractions for \(N=0\) are undefined.
Rate differences \(\Delta(j)=F(a^\star(j))-F^O(j)\) and their paired
summary use only \(n_{11}\), with that denominator explicitly reported;
if \(n_{11}=0\), the paired summary is undefined, not zero.
For infeasible NOMA, retain a failure status and undefined constrained
optimum; do not substitute zero rate. OMA's unconstrained reference rates
may still be recorded outside its feasible set, explicitly labeled, but
do not enter the accepted feasible-case comparison.

All identities and inequalities here are exact derivations. The bounded
symbolic file checks selected algebraic identities, limits and decidable
curvature cases; it cannot prove every inequality, domain branch, source
claim, or future implementation. Independent scalar-oracle validation is
proposed in algorithm.md, not executed. Numerical cancellation in
\(2^q-1\), subtraction near \(A=T_w\), overflow in products/exponentials,
and misclassification near a singleton interval must be addressed in P5.
Stable log1p/expm1 forms, scaled comparisons and higher precision are
prospective tools; tolerances, resolutions, caps and stopping criteria
remain unstated pending P5 approval. Never infer measured results from
this specification.

\section{Source attribution}
The approved scope and selected idea determine the model. Source-map.md
links the six grounded cached manuscripts with PDF page numbers and transfer
restrictions. Xu et al. (arXiv:1504.07751, pp.1--2) supports the ordered
Gaussian broadcast rate context and warns through fixed-split loss events.
Zhu et al. (DOI:10.1109/JSAC.2017.2725618, pp.3,6--7) supplies a related
boundary optimizer with extra power-order/SIC-stability restrictions that
are not imported. Oviedo and Sadjadpour's Fair-NOMA manuscript
(DOI:10.1109/TVT.2017.2689000, pp.2--3) supplies the matched OMA and
individual fairness interval context. The exact arbitrary-QoS derivation,
zero-case extensions and scoped comparison proof above are this project's
own rederivations of established principles, not copied project results
or an original contribution. No asymptotic numerical gain is asserted.
\end{document}

files.model/assumptions.yaml:
- id: A1
  statement: Each block is a two-user single-antenna scalar ordered channel, with finite 0 <= g_w <= g_s
    and nonnegative finite total P; no fading distribution is specified.
  justification: Formalizes the G1 ideal scalar benchmark and includes degenerate realizations without
    borrowing a paper distribution.
  citation: 'Approved scope.md: Proposed comparison and Boundaries; scope.yaml inclusion; G1 decision
    2ea3b17. Xu arxiv:1504.07751 cached PDF p.1 Section I supplies ordered scalar Gaussian BC context.'
  consequence_if_violated: Rate formulas, SIC-order argument and sum/feasibility theorem may fail; do
    not extrapolate to vector channels or reverse ordering.
  test_or_relaxation: P5 validation must include equal and zero gains and reject unordered invalid inputs;
    any MIMO/mobility/fading-model extension requires an explicit approved deviation.
- id: A2
  statement: Perfect instantaneous channel knowledge is available for selecting each block power split;
    overhead and estimation error are excluded.
  justification: Exact per-block optimization is the approved dry-run objective; this is an idealization
    rather than a practical CSIT assertion.
  citation: Approved scope.md Proposed comparison and Boundaries; scope.yaml inclusion; G1 decision 2ea3b17.
    QoS limits doi:10.1109/icc.2018.8422366 cached PDF p.1 discusses practical CSIT limitations, not a
    justification for inferring perfect CSI in every paper.
  consequence_if_violated: An allocation based on erroneous or delayed channels can violate QoS/SIC and
    the matched instantaneous theorem is not applicable.
  test_or_relaxation: Keep exact CSI in this benchmark; a future error model/robust allocation requires
    scope deviation and PI review.
- id: A3
  statement: 'Gaussian broadcast achievable-rate idealization: independent unit-energy codebook symbols,
    proper unit-variance complex AWGN and unit normalized bandwidth; rates are information-theoretic whole-block
    spectral efficiencies.'
  justification: Makes the approved unit-noise ideal scalar degraded broadcast rate model explicit; excludes
    finite-modulation/error-rate claims.
  citation: Approved scope.md Proposed comparison and scope.yaml ideal scalar degraded broadcast inclusion.
    Xu arxiv:1504.07751 cached PDF p.1 equation (1) and Gaussian/unit-variance description; Fair-NOMA
    doi:10.1109/tvt.2017.2689000 cached PDF p.2 Section III noise and symbol-energy normalization.
  consequence_if_violated: Physical-unit conversions or finite modulation/coding may change achievable
    rates; these equations cannot imply packet success or finite-block performance.
  test_or_relaxation: Check normalized units and P5 direct rate calculations; physical noise/bandwidth
    or finite-block extensions require separately approved models.
- id: A4
  statement: Strong receiver first decodes the weak codeword treating its own as noise, then cancels it
    perfectly; weak receiver treats strong signal as noise. Both weak decoding sites constrain the weak
    rate.
  justification: Approved ideal SIC and ordered gains make the strong weak-message capacity no smaller;
    no additional half-power or stability restriction is needed in this ideal model.
  citation: Approved scope.md Proposed comparison and scope.yaml ideal SIC inclusion. Fair-NOMA doi:10.1109/tvt.2017.2689000
    cached PDF p.2 equations (1)-(3); Ding doi:10.48550/arxiv.1412.2799 cached PDF p.2 weak-message SIC
    inequality.
  consequence_if_violated: Residual interference or decoding error invalidates strong post-SIC SINR aB and its rate log2(1+aB) and can
    break interval, optimum and OMA comparison.
  test_or_relaxation: P5 must evaluate both decoding capacities directly, including endpoints/equal gains.
    Imperfect SIC requires a new approved model, not a hidden margin.
- id: A5
  statement: Full nonnegative unit-sum power split a in [0,1], fixed arbitrary finite nonnegative individual
    QoS q_w,q_s, and unweighted sum-rate maximization per block.
  justification: Preserves G1 and selected idea-01; endpoint zero-rate allocations and unequal targets
    are legitimate.
  citation: Approved scope.md Proposed comparison; selected ideas/idea-01.yaml method_sketch and problem;
    G3 decision cb4061a. Zhu doi:10.1109/jsac.2017.2725618 cached PDF pp.3,6-7 is related context with
    extra restrictions explicitly not transferred.
  consequence_if_violated: Weights, imposed a<=1/2, positive minimum powers or different QoS notions change
    optimizer, feasibility or both.
  test_or_relaxation: P5 must cover zero targets, all endpoints and infeasible/singleton cases; new constraints/objectives
    require approved deviation.
- id: A6
  statement: OMA serves each user in exactly half of the same constant-channel block at full identical
    active-slot power P and identical unit bandwidth/noise, channels and whole-block QoS.
  justification: Matched duration/bandwidth/energy makes the intended baseline comparison well-defined.
  citation: Approved scope.md Proposed comparison and scope.yaml equal-time OMA inclusion. Fair-NOMA doi:10.1109/tvt.2017.2689000
    cached PDF pp.1-2 Section III supplies half-period full-power reference.
  consequence_if_violated: Using 2P, P/2, a different channel block, adaptive slots or unmatched QoS changes
    the fairness witness and comparison.
  test_or_relaxation: P5 must independently audit rate factor 1/2 and energy P*tau; other schedulers need
    a separately approved baseline.
- id: A7
  statement: Report all four joint feasibility categories and their denominators; accepted paired sums
    use only both-feasible blocks and no infeasible optimum is silently set to zero.
  justification: Preserves approved comparison safeguards and distinguishes rates, necessary bounds and
    feasibility.
  citation: Approved scope.md Proposed comparison; scope.yaml exclusion of ignored infeasibility; idea-01.yaml

    interference bounds and success/capacity claims.
  consequence_if_violated: Dropped failures or wrong denominators bias feasibility and rate comparisons

    produce undefined summaries, and numerical ambiguity is retained separately pending protocol handling.

# M11 numerical protocol v1

## Authorization and purpose

G4 was approved by the PI in commit 08808d8. P5 phase start passed. This is
the established, ideal scalar benchmark selected at G3, not a novelty claim.
No data have been sampled under this protocol at authoring time. Commit every
input before `lab sim lock`; run only through `lab sim run`. G5 reviews completed
experiments; P6 independently verifies results after actual G5 approval.

## Physical model and comparison

All seven G4 assumptions and predictions apply unchanged. Total normalized
power P equals linear received SNR for a unit channel gain and unit noise.
Generate two independent unit-mean exponential power gains, sort each pair
weak/strong, and reuse identical draws for all methods and diagnostics. This
is an explicit sampling choice within the approved ideal scalar model, with no
geographic path loss, antenna, estimation or coding model. Perfect CSI and ideal
SIC; bandwidth and block length normalized to one. NOMA uses the whole block
and a strong-user fraction a in [0,1]. OMA uses full P during each half-block.
Both expend energy P per block and use the same gains and per-user fixed QoS.
P is a normalized ratio, not watts or dBm. Rates are bit/s/Hz per full block.
Use the framework's dB-to-linear helper only for scenario conversion.

## Scenarios and fixed workload

Primary grid: P in {0,10,20} dB, fixed (qw,qs) in {(0,0),(.25,.25),(.5,.5)}.
Reference-only extension: (0,0) at {30,40,50} dB. Twelve MC scenarios total.
Each has seeds 11001 through 11012 and 32,768 trials per seed: 393,216 blocks
per setting. PCG64 with SeedSequence([seed,0]) supplies channels. Reusing each
seed's ordered gains across the grid is deliberate; seed streams are independent
within a scenario. No seed selection, adaptive stopping or post-result extension.
No random noise or optimizer initialization is needed for these Shannon rates.
Fixed N is a CPU-scale planning choice aiming for <=1% relative 95% CI halfwidth;
it is not a guarantee. Report any failed precision/event threshold as inconclusive.

Deterministic cases (one manifest job, 100 rows: repeat the fixed 20-case table
five times) cover zero power, zero gains, zero targets, positive targets at zero
gain, equal-gain ties, exact singleton at A=3,B=9,qw=1,qs=2, equal-gain singleton,
weak-only and strong-only QoS, clearly infeasible QoS, narrow positive/empty
intervals, tiny SNR, huge but finite SNR, and asymmetric targets. Repeated rows
are not independent samples and receive no statistical CIs. The cases are
committed in cases.yaml; no data-dependent cases are added to this run.

## Implementation, numerical uncertainty and oracle

analytic.py evaluates the approved closed form with log1p/expm1 and explicit
zero branches. Infeasible optima are undefined (NaN in raw CSV, null in JSON).
Target values, gains and P must be finite and nonnegative and gains ordered.
Binary64 intermediate overflow or unresolved near-boundary comparisons are
flagged. A tolerance cannot create mathematical feasibility or clamp an empty
interval. Integer-target ambiguous cases may use an exact rational certificate
for the binary64 inputs; noninteger ambiguous cases remain unresolved.
Record N_total, N_resolved, N_unresolved and all four joint feasibility counts.
The exact four-count identity applies to N_resolved; unresolved blocks are
preserved separately and make any unqualified full-ensemble conclusion invalid.

oracle.py is a distinct implementation: no analytic imports or copied endpoint
decision. It uses original SINRs over [0,1] and bracketed original constraints,
then a bounded objective search. Integer-target rational certificates and
conservative objective bounds, when available, are distinguished from numerical
solver agreement. Failure to settle a singleton/narrow interval is unresolved,
never infeasible merely because a grid missed it. Run it for all 100 deterministic
rows and the first 32 MC rows of every seed, without outcome-based selection.
Rerun the first eight of those rows with tolerances ten times tighter; save both.
Proposed rate tolerance 1e-9, split tolerance 1e-12, objective tolerance 1e-7;
root cap96 per constraint and bounded optimizer cap256 iterations; record actual
solver caps/statuses. These qualify numerical agreement only.
Full oracle implementation details and guaranteed domain are in the engineer
design artifact; any limits must be reported in G5, not hidden by a PASS badge.

## Metrics, denominators and diagnostics

Record original gains, targets, P, analytic candidate/split, interval bounds,
original SINRs, both weak decoding rates, strong rate, OMA individual rates,
feasibility statuses and residuals. n00: neither feasible; n01: OMA only;
n10: NOMA only; n11: both feasible. Counts must reconstruct every resolved row.
Feasibility estimates use the full resolved count, with unresolved count adjacent.
Report individual infeasibility counts as well as joint infeasibility.
Optimal NOMA sum, matched OMA sum and their paired difference are summarized
only on n11. Retain all infeasible rows; no undefined optimum becomes zero.
If n11=0 the paired mean/CI is undefined. No individual-rate dominance claim.

P1-P7 diagnostics: SIC dominance, interval membership/classification, objective
agreement, target activation, OMA-only count, paired negative-difference count,
ledger reconstruction and oracle disagreements/unresolved statuses. These are
numerical validation receipts, not finite-sample proofs of universal laws.
Two algorithm ablations use these same channels/QoS/resources: fixed a=.25 and
101-point exhaustive grid including endpoints. Record their feasibility and
objective loss relative to analytic optimum only when both allocations are
feasible. A grid miss is not a certified infeasible case. These are diagnostics
of allocation/search, not newly selected literature baselines or objectives.

## Statistical policy

Compute the paired rate mean from all both-feasible independent blocks in a
setting; conditional sampling produces independent draws from the conditional
distribution. Use a two-sided 95% Student-t CI on those paired differences and
on the two conditional sum means, n=n11 (not total draws). n<2 => undefined CI.
Cross-setting draws are paired and no cross-setting significance claims are made.
For feasibility/infeasibility counts use two-sided 95% exact binomial intervals.
At least 100 observed infeasibility events are needed for a conclusive outage
estimate. Zero events yield an upper bound, not a zero outage proof. For an
identically feasible zero-QoS analytic regime, report the mathematical reason
separately from the empirical bound. Confidence intervals are pointwise; no
familywise guarantee across the grid. Deterministic ties and zero means receive
absolute residuals, not a meaningless relative halfwidth criterion.

## OMA baseline reproduction

The selected baseline is the already approved matched equal-time OMA. Implement
it locally from Fair-NOMA (Oviedo/Sadjadpour, TVT 2017), source PDF page2,
Section III; page3 equations (6)-(8); Figure1 on page4 with beta=1. Reproduce
only its two OMA curves on {0,10,20,30,40,50} dB, using all unfiltered draws from
zero-QoS scenarios. Reference values are evaluated from the paper's exact
published equations, not invented/digitized plot coordinates:

- E[RwO] = exp(2/P) E1(2/P)/(2 ln2).
- E[RsO] = [2 exp(1/P) E1(1/P) - exp(2/P) E1(2/P)]/(2 ln2).
- E[SO] = exp(1/P) E1(1/P)/ln2.

Require <=5% relative difference, correct strong>weak ordering, both curves
increasing with P, and report observed CIs. An overlay compares MC estimates to
these exact reference curves. This is reproduction of the OMA subset of Figure1,
not the paper's channel-dependent Fair-NOMA allocation or every curve/figure.
No external code package is accepted or executed, no paper-specific half-power
constraint is imported, no publisher figure image is redistributed. Generated
synthetic data need no external dataset. Local source/dependencies are reviewed;
the framework LICENSE governs original implementation, not ownership of papers.

## Evidence and execution

Language: Python in the existing uv.lock-pinned environment; no learning/MATLAB
route required for this scalar run. Budget estimate: <=1 GB per job, 145 serial
jobs, seconds to minutes per job; runtime is measured, not promised. All input
code, fixed cases, protocol, uv.lock, framework Python/MATLAB code are locked.
Raw CSV is local and git-ignored, accessible through checksum-bound manifests.
Commit summaries, manifests, collection receipt, protocol and review artifacts.
No raw binary stores or PDFs are committed. Keep failed jobs/logs and retain
old runs if a code fix forces relock. Resume only verified complete jobs.
The raw collector is a checksum/inventory convenience: its unconditioned means
and NaNs are not the scientific summary; aggregate.py implements the declared
denominators. P6 will independently recompute before manuscript claims.

Before locking, run the unit/physics checks explicitly required by the user's
implementation plan, section5.5. Then commit inputs, lock, run/status/collect,
aggregate and reproduce the reference overlay. Request G5 with full limitations
and provenance. Do not enter P6 or approve G5 for the PI.

"""Pinned P6 recomputation; must be reviewed independently before P6 execution.

Uses original rates, a full-domain constraint bracket, and the distinct scalar
oracle. It does not import the analytic metric implementation. This module is
prepared at P5 so subsequent verification never changes locked run inputs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
from collections import defaultdict
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import oracle

from lab.io import load, save
from lab.simulation import manifest_output, verify_manifest
from lab.verification import average_ci


def rates(P, gw, gs, a):
    # Original transmit powers and received interference, independently written.
    weak_power, strong_power = P * (1 - a), P * a
    weak_sinr = weak_power * gw / (1 + strong_power * gw)
    decoding_sinr = weak_power * gs / (1 + strong_power * gs)
    strong_sinr = strong_power * gs
    return tuple(np.log1p(x) / np.log(2) for x in (weak_sinr, decoding_sinr, strong_sinr))


def bracket(P, gw, gs, qw, qs):
    n = len(gw)
    lower_lo, lower_hi = np.zeros(n), np.ones(n)
    upper_lo, upper_hi = np.zeros(n), np.ones(n)
    for _ in range(48):
        m = (lower_lo + lower_hi) / 2
        strong_ok = rates(P, gw, gs, m)[2] >= qs
        lower_hi = np.where(strong_ok, m, lower_hi)
        lower_lo = np.where(strong_ok, lower_lo, m)
        m = (upper_lo + upper_hi) / 2
        w, s, _ = rates(P, gw, gs, m)
        weak_ok = np.minimum(w, s) >= qw
        upper_lo = np.where(weak_ok, m, upper_lo)
        upper_hi = np.where(weak_ok, upper_hi, m)
    min_lower = np.where(qs == 0, 0, lower_lo)
    max_upper = np.where(qw == 0, 1, upper_hi)
    endpoint_w = rates(P, gw, gs, np.zeros(n))[0]
    endpoint_s = rates(P, gw, gs, np.ones(n))[2]
    possible = (endpoint_w >= qw) & (endpoint_s >= qs)
    margin = max_upper - min_lower
    return possible, margin


def exact_constraints(values, split):
    P, gw, gs, qw, qs = values
    if not float(qw).is_integer() or not float(qs).is_integer() or not split:
        return None
    a = Fraction(str(split))
    P, gw, gs = map(lambda x: Fraction(float(x)), (P, gw, gs))
    weak = (1 - a) * P * gw / (1 + a * P * gw)
    decode = (1 - a) * P * gs / (1 + a * P * gs)
    strong = a * P * gs
    return 0 <= a <= 1 and min(weak, decode) >= 2 ** int(qw) - 1 and strong >= 2 ** int(qs) - 1


def verify(project, output):
    output.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)
    counts = defaultdict(int)
    maxima = defaultdict(float)
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    evidence = []
    tighter_differences = []
    oracle_differences = []
    for mf in sorted((project / "results/runs").glob("*/manifest.json")):
        manifest = verify_manifest(project, load(mf))
        file = manifest_output(project, manifest, "channels.csv")
        d = np.genfromtxt(file, delimiter=",", names=True, dtype=None, encoding="utf-8")
        evidence.append(mf.relative_to(project).as_posix())
        P, gw, gs, qw, qs = [d[k] for k in ("P", "gw", "gs", "qw", "qs")]
        feasible = d["status"] == "feasible"
        a = np.where(feasible, d["a_star"], 0)
        rw, decode, rs = rates(P, gw, gs, a)
        oma_w = np.log1p(P * gw) / np.log(2) / 2
        oma_s = np.log1p(P * gs) / np.log(2) / 2
        original_sum = np.minimum(rw, decode) + rs
        counts["rows"] += len(d)
        counts["unresolved"] += int(np.sum(d["category"] == "unresolved"))
        counts["sic_violations"] += int(np.sum(feasible & (decode < rw - 1e-9)))
        counts["constraint_violations"] += int(
            np.sum(feasible & ((rw < qw - 1e-9) | (rs < qs - 1e-9)))
        )
        if np.any(feasible):
            maxima["sum_recomputation_error"] = max(
                maxima["sum_recomputation_error"],
                float(np.max(np.abs(original_sum[feasible] - d["sum_rate"][feasible]))),
            )
        active = feasible & (P * gw > 0)
        if np.any(active):
            maxima["weak_activation_error"] = max(
                maxima["weak_activation_error"], float(np.max(np.abs(rw[active] - qw[active])))
            )
        maxima["oma_recomputation_error"] = max(
            maxima["oma_recomputation_error"], float(np.max(np.abs(oma_w + oma_s - d["oma_sum"])))
        )
        counts["oma_only"] += int(np.sum(d["category"] == "n01"))
        both = d["category"] == "n11"
        counts["negative_paired"] += int(np.sum(both & (original_sum - oma_w - oma_s < -1e-9)))
        possible, margin = bracket(P, gw, gs, qw, qs)
        separated = np.abs(margin) > 1e-9
        root_feasible = possible & (margin > 0)
        decided = d["status"] != "unresolved"
        counts["bracket_disagreements"] += int(
            np.sum(separated & decided & (root_feasible != feasible))
        )
        for j in np.flatnonzero(d["certificate"] == "exact-rational"):
            if feasible[j] and not exact_constraints(
                [x[j] for x in (P, gw, gs, qw, qs)], str(d["exact_split"][j])
            ):
                counts["exact_certificate_failures"] += 1
        for u, v in ((0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)):
            expected = (d["feasible"] == u) & (d["oma_feasible"] == v)
            counts["ledger_disagreements"] += int(np.sum(expected != (d["category"] == f"n{u}{v}")))
        counts["undefined_optimum_violations"] += int(
            np.sum(~feasible & np.isfinite(d["sum_rate"]))
        )
        if manifest.params["kind"] != "deterministic":
            groups[manifest.scenario].append(d)
        for checked in load(manifest_output(project, manifest, "oracle.json"))["checks"]:
            j = checked["row"]
            independently_repeated = oracle.solve(*checked["inputs"])
            old = checked["oracle"]
            counts["oracle_status_disagreements"] += int(
                independently_repeated["status"] != old["status"]
            )
            oracle_value = independently_repeated.get("sum_rate")
            if feasible[j] and oracle_value is not None and math.isfinite(oracle_value):
                oracle_differences.append(abs(float(d["sum_rate"][j]) - oracle_value))
            tighter = checked.get("tighter_oracle")
            if tighter and old.get("sum_rate") is not None and tighter.get("sum_rate") is not None:
                tighter_differences.append(abs(old["sum_rate"] - tighter["sum_rate"]))
    precision = {}
    for scenario, parts in groups.items():
        d = np.concatenate(parts)
        mask = d["category"] == "n11"
        precision[scenario] = {}
        for name in ("sum_rate", "oma_sum", "paired_difference"):
            values = d[name][mask]
            summary = average_ci(values) if len(values) >= 2 else None
            precision[scenario][name] = summary
    all_precision = all(
        v is not None and v["relative_halfwidth"] <= 0.01
        for s in precision.values()
        for v in s.values()
    )
    checks_boolean = {

"""Independent original-SINR constraint search over the full split domain.

No analytic-module imports, closed-form QoS endpoints, or derivative-sign
optimizer. Rational feasibility certificates and numerical objective checks
are explicitly different evidence. Numerical secant bounds are not rigorous
interval arithmetic certificates.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction

from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar


def direct_rates(P, gw, gs, a):
    """Original decoding-site SINRs, independently implemented scalar path."""
    if not all(math.isfinite(x) and x >= 0 for x in (P, gw, gs)):
        raise ValueError("Power and gains must be finite nonnegative scalars")
    if gw > gs or not math.isfinite(a) or not 0 <= a <= 1:
        raise ValueError("Ordered gains and split in [0,1] required")
    received_w, received_s = P * gw, P * gs
    weak_at_w = (1 - a) * received_w / (1 + a * received_w)
    weak_at_s = (1 - a) * received_s / (1 + a * received_s)
    strong_after_sic = a * received_s
    capacity_w = math.log1p(weak_at_w) / math.log(2)
    capacity_sic = math.log1p(weak_at_s) / math.log(2)
    strong = math.log1p(strong_after_sic) / math.log(2)
    return {
        "gamma_ww": weak_at_w,
        "gamma_ws": weak_at_s,
        "gamma_ss": strong_after_sic,
        "rw_site": capacity_w,
        "cw_at_s": capacity_sic,
        "rw": min(capacity_w, capacity_sic),
        "rs": strong,
        "sum_rate": min(capacity_w, capacity_sic) + strong,
    }


def _exact_constraints(P, gw, gs, qw, qs):
    # The only target conversion here is the exact integer 2**q-1. Constraints
    # are evaluated as original SINRs; there is no endpoint formula.
    if not (qw.is_integer() and qs.is_integer() and max(qw, qs) <= 1024):
        return None
    power, weak, strong = map(Fraction, (P, gw, gs))
    received_w, received_s = power * weak, power * strong
    target_w, target_s = 2 ** int(qw) - 1, 2 ** int(qs) - 1

    def residuals(a):
        at_w = (1 - a) * received_w / (1 + a * received_w) - target_w
        at_s = (1 - a) * received_s / (1 + a * received_s) - target_w
        post_sic = a * received_s - target_s
        return min(at_w, at_s), post_sic

    return residuals


def _bracket(predicate, increasing, zero, one, tolerance, cap):
    """Bracket a monotone constraint threshold from original-domain endpoints.

    Returned inner and outer bounds retain the true threshold for exact
    predicates. Float predicates provide numerical bracketing only.
    """
    at_zero, at_one = predicate(zero), predicate(one)
    if increasing:
        if at_zero:
            return zero, zero, 0, True
        if not at_one:
            return None, None, 0, True
    else:
        if at_one:
            return one, one, 0, True
        if not at_zero:
            return None, None, 0, True
    left, right = zero, one
    for count in range(1, cap + 1):
        midpoint = (left + right) / 2
        if midpoint == left or midpoint == right:
            return left, right, count, True
        satisfied = predicate(midpoint)
        if satisfied == increasing:
            right = midpoint
        else:
            left = midpoint
        if float(right - left) <= tolerance:
            return left, right, count, True
    return left, right, cap, False


def _rational_witness(residuals, brackets):
    """Try rational reconstruction, then check original SINRs exactly.

    Reconstruction is a search heuristic. The exact direct check supplies the
    certificate. Simultaneously active weak/strong constraints certify a
    singleton by their monotone QoS sets, without endpoint algebra.
    """
    candidates = {Fraction(0), Fraction(1)}
    for x in brackets:
        for denominator in (1024, 65536, 1000000, 2**32):
            candidates.add(x.limit_denominator(denominator))
    for candidate in sorted(candidates):
        if 0 <= candidate <= 1:
            w, s = residuals(candidate)
            if w >= 0 and s >= 0:
                return candidate, w == 0 and s == 0
    return None, False


def _concavity_upper_bound(objective, low, high, best_x, best_f, split_tolerance):
    """Numerical supporting-line envelope from direct objective secants.

    For exact concave f, the left secant at t upper bounds slopes to its
    right and the right secant lower bounds slopes to its left. Floating
    evaluation and finite secants receive a roundoff allowance, not a formal
    validated-numerics error proof.
    """
    width = high - low
    if width <= 0:
        return best_f, 0.0
    h = min(width / 4, max(4 * split_tolerance, width * 1e-5))
    center = min(max(best_x, low + h), high - h)
    left, right = center - h, center + h
    if not low <= left < center < right <= high:
        return math.nan, math.nan
    fl, ft, fr = objective(left), objective(center), objective(right)
    slope_left, slope_right = (ft - fl) / (center - left), (fr - ft) / (right - center)
    upper_left = ft + max(0.0, slope_right * (low - center))
    upper_right = ft + max(0.0, slope_left * (high - center))
    roundoff_allowance = 256 * math.ulp(max(1.0, abs(fl), abs(ft), abs(fr), abs(best_f)))
    upper = max(best_f, upper_left, upper_right) + roundoff_allowance
    return upper, max(0.0, upper - best_f)


def solve(
    P,
    gw,
    gs,
    qw,
    qs,
    *,
    rate_tolerance=1e-9,
    split_tolerance=1e-12,
    objective_tolerance=1e-7,
    max_root_iterations=96,
    max_optimizer_iterations=256,

    comparisons. Objective optimality is always numerical (except a proved
    singleton/constant zero domain); a SciPy success flag alone is insufficient.

        math.isfinite(x) and x > 0 for x in (rate_tolerance, split_tolerance, objective_tolerance)
    ):

        type(max_root_iterations) is not int

        or type(max_optimizer_iterations) is not int

        "feasibility_certificate": "none",
        "optimality_status": "not-established",
        "a_star": math.nan,
        "candidate_a": math.nan,
        "exact_split": "",

        "residual_s": math.nan,
        "sic_residual": math.nan,

                feasible=0.0,
                reason="Original endpoint capacity cannot satisfy a QoS constraint",
            )
        else:
            result["reason"] = "Endpoint feasibility inside numerical rate band"
        return result
    weak_inner, weak_outer = weak[0], weak[1]
    strong_outer, strong_inner = strong[0], strong[1]
    result.update(
        inner_lower=float(strong_inner),
        inner_upper=float(weak_inner),
        outer_lower=float(strong_outer),
        outer_upper=float(weak_outer),

    elif strong_inner <= weak_inner and (
        exact is not None or float(weak_inner - strong_inner) > 2 * split_tolerance
    ):

        result["exact_split"] = str(witness)

        result["reason"] = "Narrow/singleton domain without an exact direct certificate"

        result["reason"] = "Certified inner interval not representable in binary64"

        return direct_rates(P, gw, gs, a)["sum_rate"]

    candidates = [low, high]
    solver_ok = True
    if low < high:
        answer = minimize_scalar(
            lambda a: -objective(a),
            bounds=(low, high),
            method="bounded",
            options={"xatol": split_tolerance, "maxiter": max_optimizer_iterations},
        )
        result["optimizer_iterations"] = int(answer.nit)
        result["optimizer_evaluations"] = int(answer.nfev)
        solver_ok = bool(answer.success)
        if math.isfinite(answer.x) and low <= answer.x <= high:

        status="feasible",
        feasible=1.0,
        a_star=best,

        optimality_status="exact-singleton" if singleton else "numerical-concavity-bound",
        reason="Original constraints and bounded scalar objective check accepted",

        receipt["source_hashes"] = before

            exc.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            if isinstance(exc.stdout, bytes)

        )
        stderr = (
            exc.stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

    raw.update(
        row="0",
        case_id="fixture",
        status=status,
        feasible=str(float(feasible)) if status != "unresolved" else "nan",
        certificate="none" if status == "unresolved" else "binary64-separated",
        A=str(v[0] * v[1]),
        B=str(v[0] * v[2]),
        exact_split="",
        boundary_flag=str(ns["low"] is not None and abs(ns["high"] - ns["low"]) <= ind.SPLIT),
        numeric_domain="True",
        candidate_violation="False",
        singleton=str(ns.get("singleton", False)),
        optimizer_unique=str(feasible and (v[1] != v[2] or ns.get("singleton", False))),
        nonunique=str(feasible and v[1] == v[2] and not ns.get("singleton", False)),
        oma_status=os,
        oma_feasible=str(float(os == "feasible")) if os != "unresolved" else "nan",
        oma_certificate="none" if os == "unresolved" else "binary64-separated",
    )
    # Boundary fields for fixtures selected to have a resolved full-domain bracket.
    raw["interval_lower"] = str(ns["low"] if ns["low"] is not None else 0.0)
    raw["interval_upper"] = str(ns["high"] if ns["high"] is not None else 1.0)
    od = ind.oma(v)
    raw.update({k: str(x) for k, x in od.items()})
    raw["oma_boundary_flag"] = str(
        any(
            q > 0 and abs(od[k]) <= ind.RATE
            for q, k in zip(v[3:], ("oma_residual_w", "oma_residual_s"))
        )
    )
    raw["category"] = ind.category(status, os)
    if feasible:
        a = ns["high"]
        rd = ind.rates(v, a)
        raw["a_star"] = raw["candidate_a"] = str(a)
        for k, x in rd.items():
            raw[k] = raw["candidate_" + k] = str(x)
        raw.update(
            residual_w=str(rd["rw"] - v[3]),
            residual_s=str(rd["rs"] - v[4]),
            sic_residual=str(rd["cw_at_s"] - rd["rw"]),
        )
        raw["candidate_constraints_pass"] = str(rd["rw"] >= v[3] and rd["rs"] >= v[4])
        raw["candidate_within_rate_tolerance"] = "True"
        raw["paired_difference"] = (
            str(rd["sum_rate"] - od["oma_sum"]) if raw["category"] == "n11" else "nan"
        )
    else:
        for k in ind.FIELDS:
            raw[k] = raw["candidate_" + k] = "nan"
        for k in (
            "a_star",
            "candidate_a",
            "residual_w",
            "residual_s",
            "sic_residual",
            "paired_difference",
        ):
            raw[k] = "nan"
        raw["candidate_constraints_pass"] = raw["candidate_within_rate_tolerance"] = "False"
    ab = ind.ablations(v)
    for k in ("fixed_feasible", "fixed_sum", "grid_found_feasible", "grid_sum"):
        raw[k] = str(ab[k])
    raw["grid_a"] = str(ab["grid_ties"][0]) if ab["grid_ties"] else "nan"
    metric = {k: raw[k] for k in ind.METRIC_COLUMNS}
    return raw, metric

def review_original_rates(inputs, a):
    """Test-only physics derived directly from the approved receiver equations."""
    P, gw, gs, _, _ = inputs
    weak_power, strong_power = P * (1 - a), P * a
    ww = weak_power * gw / (1 + strong_power * gw)
    ws = weak_power * gs / (1 + strong_power * gs)
    ss = strong_power * gs
    rw_site, cw_at_s, rs = map(lambda x: math.log2(1 + x), (ww, ws, ss))
    rw = min(rw_site, cw_at_s)
    return dict(
        gamma_ww=ww,
        gamma_ws=ws,
        gamma_ss=ss,
        rw_site=rw_site,
        cw_at_s=cw_at_s,
        rw=rw,
        rs=rs,
        sum_rate=rw + rs,
    )


def review_rewrite_final(raw, metric, inputs, a):
    """Make a coherent scientific corruption, rather than just changing a flag."""
    r = review_original_rates(inputs, a)
    raw["a_star"] = raw["candidate_a"] = str(a)
    for k, value in r.items():
        raw[k] = raw["candidate_" + k] = str(value)
    raw["residual_w"] = str(r["rw"] - inputs[3])
    raw["residual_s"] = str(r["rs"] - inputs[4])
    raw["sic_residual"] = str(r["cw_at_s"] - r["rw"])
    raw["candidate_constraints_pass"] = str(r["rw"] >= inputs[3] and r["rs"] >= inputs[4])
    raw["candidate_within_rate_tolerance"] = str(
        r["rw"] >= inputs[3] - ind.RATE and r["rs"] >= inputs[4] - ind.RATE
    )
    raw["candidate_violation"] = str(min(r["rw"] - inputs[3], r["rs"] - inputs[4]) < -ind.RATE)
    if raw["category"] == "n11":
        # Independent matched OMA half-block rates, without the production helper.
        oma_sum = sum(math.log2(1 + inputs[0] * g) / 2 for g in inputs[1:3])
        raw["paired_difference"] = str(r["sum_rate"] - oma_sum)
    for k in ind.METRIC_COLUMNS:
        metric[k] = raw[k]

def synthetic_replay(base_split=1.0, tighter_split=1.0, status="feasible", inputs=None):

    params = dict(
        oracle_rows=1,

    def solve(*values, **policy):

            oracle=base,
            tighter_oracle=tight,
        )
    ]
    return checks, [raw], params, solve
